overall: The AG found the Chicopee City Council violated the Open Meeting Law by discussing non-litigation topics in an August 2011 executive session, with inadequate notice and chair statements, and ordered compliance, minutes revision, and a 30-day minutes review.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Council's August 23, 2011 executive session on pending litigation was improper because the notice and chair's statement omitted the litigating-position declaration.
allegations.key_passage: Although parts of the Council's discussion with the Law Department during the August 23, 2011 executive session were appropriate under Purpose 3, significant portions of the conversation were not.

allegations.summary: Meeting notice said only 'to discuss pending litigation'; the AG found it did not list topics with sufficient specificity, though the complainant had not raised this.
allegations.key_passage: The meeting notice should have specifically stated the names of all pending litigation matters that the Council anticipated discussing during the executive session, if doing so would not have compromised the purposes for the executive session.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the chair failed to state the executive session purpose adequately before convening; the AG found the general statement insufficient.
allegations.key_passage: The Chair's general statement that the Council would go into executive session "for the purpose of discussing pending litigation" failed this requirement as well.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the chair did not state that an open meeting may have a detrimental effect on the Council's litigating position before entering executive session.
allegations.key_passage: Furthermore, the Chair failed to make the statement required by Purpose 3 that an open meeting would have a detrimental effect on the litigating position of the public body.

allegations.summary: Council discussed Law Department staffing, general areas of law, and city property use in executive session, which the AG found outside the litigation purpose cited.
allegations.key_passage: Discussions relating to Law Department personnel, unrelated to any pending or imminently threatened litigation, are clearly not appropriate for executive session under Purpose 3.

allegations.summary: Executive session minutes omitted significant discussion subjects, including areas of law unrelated to pending litigation.
allegations.key_passage: Finally, we note that significant portions of the discussion, such as the discussion of certain areas of law that were unrelated to any pending action, were omitted from the executive session minutes.

remedy: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and caution the Council that a determination by our office of similar violations in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
In addition, we order the Council to revise the executive session minutes to include a summary of the discussion on each subject discussed.

Furthermore, we order the Council to review the minutes from the August 23, 2011 executive session and: (1) release all portions that were not appropriate for discussion under executive session Purpose 3, unless the attorney-client privilege or an exemption to the Public Records Law applies; (2) determine whether continued non-disclosure of the portions of the discussion that were appropriate under Purpose 3 is warranted, and publicly announce that determination during an open session meeting.
